surfaces.part: left cliff cut wall (brown, dark edge line)

answer.evidence: The main body is a dirt ramp surface with a continuous noisy texture over all 64 rows (width 48). It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no south face below it. The column scans show only scattered lighter and darker texture pixels, not a band or an edge line. The only vertical faces are the narrow brown (left) and orange (right) cliff-cut side walls at the edges, rows 2-47, and the left one has a dark inner edge line. The ramp itself reads as a sloped plane seen from above with no front face of 3 or more rows, so it is a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a soil ramp with speckled grain across the whole surface. It has about 5 soil steps, plus dark-brown and lighter orange-brown edge strips and grass corners at the bottom. Measured facts support this. It has 9 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the edges lean brown beside the soil rather than forming a black sticker outline. The grain is fairly uniform and lacks the per-clump variety of the Beodeul grass, which keeps texture at 'some' rather than 'rich'. Overall it sits at or above the references in density and would not look thinner or flatter beside them.
